data.best_text: May to September when Tivoli is open and people eat outdoors, December for the Christmas markets.
data.day_budget_note: Per person per day excluding flights: a share of a mid-range double room, food, local transport and one sight. A rough estimate.

stay.label: Weekend
stay.text: Nyhavn, Tivoli and a tower with a view.

stay.label: Long weekend
stay.text: Time to cycle around, eat your way through Vesterbro and take a canal tour.

stay.label: Five days
stay.text: Add a day trip by train, for example Louisiana or Helsingør.

areas.name: Vesterbro
areas.text: Close to the central station and Tivoli, with the city's densest choice of food and bars.

areas.name: Indre By
areas.text: Walking distance to everything. The most expensive area.

areas.name: Nørrebro
areas.text: Younger and cheaper, with the metro into the centre.

areas.name: The blocks right behind the central station
areas.text: Rowdy at night along Istedgade closest to the station. Choose a couple of blocks further into Vesterbro.

transport.text: About 13 minutes to Kongens Nytorv. The metro runs around the clock.

events.name: Distortion
events.text: Street parties in a new district each day, and a two-day festival by the harbour at the end.

events.name: Copenhagen Jazz Festival
events.text: Concerts in squares, parks and clubs all over the city. The dates come from a travel guide, not from the festival itself.

seasons.name: Tivoli, summer season
seasons.text: In 2026 the park was open from 7 April to 20 September.

seasons.name: Swimming in the harbour
seasons.text: The harbour baths open on 1 June.

seasons.name: Christmas in Tivoli and Christmas markets

month_notes: Cold, windy and dark. Tivoli is closed.
Still winter. The cheapest time to stay.
Spring begins, but the wind is cold.
Tivoli opens for the season. The weather can turn.
Bright and green. The outdoor tables at Nyhavn fill up.
Long evenings and swimming in the harbour.
High summer. The warmest water and the most tourists.
Dark and raw before the Christmas season.
Christmas markets and Christmas at Tivoli. Dark early.

prices.summary: More expensive than at home, above all in restaurants and for beer and coffee.
tips: A double room costs around 320 dollars per night on average according to Kayak. The source gives no breakdown by hotel class.

DK-fakta-inresa.title: Passport or national ID card
DK-fakta-inresa.summary: Bring a passport or national ID card. A driving licence does not normally count as a travel document.
DK-fakta-inresa.body: A national ID card is valid for travel within the EU and Schengen, which also includes Iceland and Norway. Within the Nordics a Swedish driving licence can be enough in some cases, but a passport or national ID card is recommended.

DK-fakta-mobil.title: Use data and call as at home
DK-fakta-mobil.summary: The same price as in Sweden for calls, texts and data.
DK-fakta-mobil.body: The EU's roaming rules apply: you pay as at home, but the operator may set a cap on data abroad.

DK-fakta-betala.title: Currency: Danish krone (DKK)
DK-fakta-betala.summary: The country uses the Danish krone (DKK).

DK-fakta-alkohol-16.title: Beer and cider from age 16 in shops
DK-fakta-alkohol-16.summary: 16–17-year-olds may buy drinks of up to 6 per cent in shops.
DK-fakta-alkohol-16.body: Since 1 April 2025 the limit is 6 per cent instead of 16.5. It applies to each individual product.

DK-fakta-alkohol-18.title: Wine and spirits from age 18
DK-fakta-alkohol-18.summary: Everything above 6 per cent requires age 18.
DK-fakta-alkohol-18.body: Drinks stronger than 6 per cent may only be sold to those aged 18 or over. In practice that means all wine and all spirits.

DK-kopenhamn-fakta-ta-sig-dit.title: Airport to the centre in 13 minutes
DK-kopenhamn-fakta-ta-sig-dit.summary: Metro M2 runs to Kongens Nytorv in about 13 minutes.
DK-kopenhamn-fakta-ta-sig-dit.body: The metro station is at Terminal 3. The line also stops at Christianshavn and Nørreport.

DK-fakta-varldsarv.title: The rune stones came first
DK-fakta-varldsarv.summary: The Jelling monuments became Denmark's first World Heritage Site in 1994.
DK-fakta-varldsarv.body: They were followed by Roskilde Cathedral in 1995 and Kronborg in 2000.

DK-kronborg.name: Kronborg
DK-kronborg.summary: The castle in Helsingør, a World Heritage Site since 2000.
DK-kronborg.body: Located at the narrowest part of the Øresund, opposite Helsingborg.

DK-roskilde-domkyrka.name: Roskilde Cathedral
DK-roskilde-domkyrka.body: The church in Roskilde, west of Copenhagen.

DK-jelling.name: The Jelling monuments
DK-jelling.summary: Burial mounds, rune stones and a church, a World Heritage Site since 1994.

DK-stevns-klint.name: Stevns Klint
DK-stevns-klint.summary: A chalk cliff on Zealand, a World Heritage Site since 2014.
DK-stevns-klint.body: A natural heritage site south of Copenhagen.

DK-vadehavet.name: The Wadden Sea
DK-vadehavet.summary: The Danish part became a World Heritage Site in 2014.
DK-vadehavet.body: A tidal landscape along the west coast of Jutland, shared with Germany and the Netherlands.

DK-kopenhamn-nyhavn.name: Nyhavn
DK-kopenhamn-nyhavn.summary: The harbour quarter at Kongens Nytorv.
DK-kopenhamn-nyhavn.body: Get off the metro at Kongens Nytorv, and Nyhavn and Strøget are right there.

DK-kopenhamn-tivoli.name: Tivoli
DK-kopenhamn-tivoli.summary: An amusement park from 1843 that is only open during its seasons.
DK-kopenhamn-tivoli.body: Open during Easter, summer, Halloween and Christmas, closed in between. The 2026 Christmas season runs 13 November–31 December, closed on Christmas Eve. Rides cost extra on top of admission.

DK-kopenhamn-christiansborg-tornet.name: The tower at Christiansborg
DK-kopenhamn-christiansborg-tornet.summary: A free view from 106 metres, the highest in the city.
DK-kopenhamn-christiansborg-tornet.body: The lift up is free, but you go through a security check like at an airport.

DK-kopenhamn-rundetarn.name: The Round Tower
DK-kopenhamn-rundetarn.summary: The tower with a spiral ramp instead of stairs.
DK-kopenhamn-rundetarn.body: The ramp is 209 metres long. Admission costs a small sum.

mat-smorrebrod.name: Smørrebrød
mat-smorrebrod.hint: An open sandwich on rye bread with generous toppings.

mat-rod-polse.name: Rød pølse
mat-rod-polse.hint: A red sausage from a pølsevogn, a hot dog stand.

bakverk-wienerbrod.name: Danish pastry
bakverk-wienerbrod.hint: The Danes call it wienerbrød, the rest of the world a Danish.

bakverk-flodeboller.name: Flødebolle
bakverk-flodeboller.hint: Marshmallow foam on a base, dipped in chocolate.

fardmedel-lastcykel.name: Cargo bike
fardmedel-lastcykel.hint: A bicycle with a large box at the front, often with children in it.

DK-kopenhamn-ide-nyhavn.title: Nyhavn and Strøget on foot
DK-kopenhamn-ide-nyhavn.body: Start at Kongens Nytorv and walk along the quay.

DK-kopenhamn-ide-kronborg.title: Kronborg in Helsingør
DK-kopenhamn-ide-kronborg.body: The castle that is a World Heritage Site. Can be combined with the ferry across to Helsingborg.

DK-kopenhamn-ide-roskilde.title: Roskilde Cathedral
DK-kopenhamn-ide-roskilde.body: A World Heritage Site west of the city.

DK-kopenhamn-ide-torn.title: Two towers in one afternoon
DK-kopenhamn-ide-torn.body: A free view from Christiansborg and the spiral ramp in the Round Tower.

DK-kopenhamn-ide-jul-i-tivoli.title: Christmas in Tivoli
DK-kopenhamn-ide-jul-i-tivoli.body: Go one evening when the lights are on. Check the season dates first, the park is closed between seasons.

DK-kopenhamn-ide-helg.title: Copenhagen over the weekend
DK-kopenhamn-ide-helg.body: Nyhavn and the towers on the first day, Tivoli in the evening and Kronborg or Roskilde on day two.

DK-present-lakrits.name: Danish liquorice
DK-present-lakrits.body: Comes in everything from bags to gift tins.

DK-present-porslin.name: Blue and white Danish porcelain
DK-present-porslin.body: A mug is the easiest to get home in one piece.

DK-present-lego.name: Lego
DK-present-lego.body: Danish from the start. Look for sets sold only in the brand store.
